evals.name: full-interview-answer
evals.prompt: Design a news feed system for 10 million DAU where users have up to 5,000 friends. Walk me through it like a 45-minute interview.
evals.expected_output: A scoped answer: clarifying assumptions, an estimate table produced by the calculator, API and data model, two flows (publishing, retrieval), a fan-out deep dive with the hybrid celebrity approach, and a wrap-up with bottlenecks, each citing Vol. 1 ch. 11.
expectations: Starts by listing functional and non-functional requirements and explicit assumptions before proposing components.
Runs scripts/estimate.py (or reproduces its table) for QPS and storage rather than doing arithmetic in prose.
Describes both feed publishing and feed retrieval flows.
Explains fan-out on write vs fan-out on read and recommends the hybrid approach for celebrities.
Cites Vol. 1 ch. 11 (or 'chapter 11') for the fan-out recommendation.
Ends with a wrap-up naming bottlenecks, failure modes and open questions.

evals.name: mock-interviewer
evals.prompt: Be my interviewer. Give me a system design question and don't tell me the answer; push back on my choices.
evals.expected_output: One problem statement, scope answers with concrete numbers when asked, no solution revealed, prompts for estimates and a deep dive, and a graded debrief at the end.
expectations: Poses a single system design problem in one or two sentences.
Does not present the architecture or solution unprompted.
Answers scope questions with concrete numbers (users, QPS, retention) the way the chapters do.
Asks the candidate for back-of-the-envelope estimates.
Offers a debrief structured by the framework's steps and dos/don'ts.
